overview: Vital Healthcare Property Trust is an NZX-listed unit trust and the only specialist healthcare-property landlord on the exchange, owning a ~$3.4-3.6 billion portfolio of 33 private hospitals, ambulatory care and life-sciences facilities across New Zealand and mainland Australia. The Trust earns long-dated rental income from hospital operators and healthcare tenants under structured, CPI-linked leases, and pursues a hospital-focused development pipeline to grow and renew the portfolio. Management was internalised on 31 December 2025, ending a long-running external management arrangement with Canadian-listed Northwest Healthcare Properties REIT (TSX: NWH.UN).

business_model.summary: Vital collects rental income from healthcare operators (hospitals, ambulatory/day-surgery clinics, life sciences) under long leases with a portfolio WALE of ~19 years, ~63% of income CPI-linked and ~26% linked to periodic market rent reviews. Growth comes from structured rent escalations, leasing/occupancy gains, and a committed/potential development pipeline (~$2.2bn) funded via divestments, debt and equity. Distributable income is reported as AFFO (Adjusted Funds From Operations); reported net profit is highly volatile because it includes non-cash investment-property fair-value revaluations and interest-rate/FX derivative mark-to-market movements.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - private hospital operators, healthcare groups and ambulatory/specialist clinic tenants (Aurora Healthcare, Healthe Care, Evolution Healthcare, Epworth HealthCare, Southern Cross, GenesisCare, Allevia, and others)
business_model.geographic_mix: Australia ~67% of portfolio value (NSW, Victoria, Queensland, South Australia, Western Australia, Tasmania, Northern Territory), New Zealand ~33% (predominantly North Island)

main_competitors: Northwest Healthcare Properties REIT (TSX: NWH.UN) - former manager, global healthcare REIT peer
Healthscope / other private hospital operator-owned real estate
HMC Capital / Healthco Healthcare and Wellness REIT (ASX)
Generic diversified Australasian REITs competing for institutional capital (Precinct, Goodman, Stockland, Charter Hall)
Private equity and sovereign wealth healthcare-property investors in Australia
competitive_position.market_position: Largest and only NZX-listed specialist healthcare-property REIT; one of the leading dedicated hospital-property owners in the Australasian market with a portfolio WALE (19 years) longer than any other NZX- or ASX-listed REIT

moat_factors.factor: Specialist asset class / high barriers to entry
moat_factors.description: Purpose-built hospital and clinical facilities require specialised design, regulatory compliance and clinical fit-out; few landlords have the expertise or relationships to develop and manage this stock

moat_factors.factor: Long lease terms and structured rent reviews
moat_factors.description: ~19-year WALE with CPI-linked/market rent reviews locks in long-duration, escalating income and high switching costs for hospital operators (clinical relocation is costly and disruptive)

moat_factors.factor: Tenant/operator relationships and development track record
moat_factors.description: Long-standing partnerships with major private hospital groups (Aurora, Healthe Care, Evolution, Epworth) and an established Trans-Tasman development platform support repeat business and precinct expansion
33 properties across two countries and multiple sub-sectors (acute hospitals, specialty hospitals, ambulatory care) reduces single-asset/tenant risk, though top-5 tenants still ~65% of rent

weaknesses: High tenant concentration - top 5 tenants represent ~65% of portfolio rent (Aurora 17%, Healthe Care 17%, Evolution 15%, Epworth 14%, Southern Cross 4%)
Small market capitalisation and limited liquidity versus ASX-listed healthcare REIT peers
High leverage (gearing ~40-42%) increases sensitivity to interest rates and cap rate movements
Newly internalised management platform - unproven as a standalone operator after decades under Northwest
Dependent on external capital markets (debt and equity) to fund its development pipeline

growth_drivers: Committed and potential development pipeline of ~$2.2 billion, including Coomera Stage 1 (Queensland, activated Feb 2026) and Macarthur Stage 2 (~A$95m, under evaluation)
Structured rent reviews - ~63% of income CPI-linked, ~26% market-reviewed - driving like-for-like NPI growth (+4.0% HY26, +3.7% FY25, +9% FY26 full year)
Leasing/occupancy improvement - occupancy lifted to 99.0% (HY26) / 97.2% (FY26) with WALE extended to 19.0 years
Internalised management platform expected to be efficient, scalable and fee-accretive, with potential new fee income via capital partnerships over time
Capital recycling - divestment of non-core/lower-growth assets (~$272m since FY23, $97.9m in HY26) reinvested into higher-quality developments
Secular healthcare demand tailwinds - ageing populations, rising healthcare spend, constrained public health systems, growth in private health insurance

business.description: Top 5 tenants ~65% of rent; financial distress at a major operator (e.g., historical pressure at some Australian private hospital groups) could impair income security

Property valuations are highly sensitive to capitalisation rate movements; FY23/FY24/FY25 all recorded unrealised revaluation losses ($208.6m, $165.2m, $96.7m respectively) versus large gains in FY21/FY22 ($235.4m, $244.2m), driving swings in reported net profit and NTA per unit (down from $3.34 in FY22 to $2.34 at Dec-25)
Large committed pipeline (~$2.2bn) carries construction cost, leasing (e.g., RDX Gold Coast ramp-up not yet at NOI guarantee level) and timing risk
First full year operating without Northwest's global platform and back-office; new internal team must prove it can match prior execution on developments, leasing and capital management

financial.description: Balance sheet gearing of ~39.6-42.1% (per Trust Deed) is high for a REIT and leaves limited headroom in a rising-rate or falling-valuation environment; debt headroom was $154.2m at Dec-25
All-in weighted cost of debt ~5.01%, weighted debt duration only ~3.3 years and hedging term ~2.6 years; ~18% of debt unhedged; net interest expense has risen steadily (FY21 $27.7m to FY25 $45.2m)

~67% of the portfolio (and a growing share of income) is AUD-denominated against NZD reporting/distribution currency; FX derivative and translation reserve movements add volatility to reported equity and profit

$214m (net ~$177m after tax) one-off internalisation payment to Northwest funded partly by a $235m equity raise (placement at $1.95, UPP at $1.9124) diluted NTA per unit ~6% and drove a large one-off HY26 accounting loss

regulatory.description: NZ and Australian government healthcare funding policy, private health insurance rebate settings, and public hospital capacity decisions influence tenant demand and viability
FY25 result flagged increased tax expense 'following law changes'; REIT/trust tax treatment changes in NZ or Australia could affect distributable income
Hospital-grade developments face stringent building code, health facility design and consenting requirements that can delay or add cost to the pipeline

macro.description: REIT sector highly rate-sensitive; higher-for-longer rates increase funding costs and can pressure cap rates/valuations further
A downturn could reduce private health insurance uptake and elective procedure volumes, pressuring tenant EBITDAR and rent affordability (targeted at ≤50% rent/EBITDAR)
Although moderating per FY25/FY26 commentary, elevated construction costs affect development economics and yields on cost

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Healthcare property is viewed as a defensive, needs-based real estate sub-sector with structural tailwinds from ageing populations, rising healthcare spend and constrained public health capacity in both New Zealand and Australia; commentary in FY25/FY26 filings notes valuations and Australian operator conditions are stabilising after a period of cap-rate softening and operator margin pressure
macro_factors.cyclicality: Lower than broader commercial/retail property due to long leases and non-discretionary tenant demand, but still exposed to interest-rate-driven cap rate cycles and REIT sector sentiment
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - ~40% gearing, weighted debt duration of only ~3.3 years and partial hedging (~80-82%) mean funding costs and valuations both move materially with rates

recent_developments.event: Vital presented at the NZ Health Design Council conference on private-public healthcare collaboration

Announced internalisation of management from Northwest Healthcare Properties REIT for ~NZ$214m consideration, alongside a NZ$235m equity raising ($190m placement at $1.95/unit + $45m unit purchase plan at $1.9124/unit)
Internalisation of management completed; Vital Healthcare Properties Management Limited (VHPML), a wholly owned Vital subsidiary, replaced Northwest as manager; net after-tax cost to Vital of ~$177m

HY26 interim result: NPI up 4.7% (4.0% like-for-like), AFFO per unit up 13.7% to 5.64cpu, occupancy 99.0%, WALE 19.0 years; large accounting loss (-$74.0m, -10.45cps) driven by the internalisation expense; NTA per unit fell to $2.34 from $2.47 at Jun-25; RDX Gold Coast (A$134.2m) reached practical completion in Feb-26; Coomera Stage 1 (A$46.6m) development activated
Q3 FY26 update: results tracking slightly ahead of expectations, aided by AUD strength (69% of properties by value in Australia); 9-month AFFO per unit 8.85cpu vs 7.78cpu pcp; gearing 39.6%

FY26 full-year result: net property income up 9% to $162.2m, AFFO up 23.5% to $86.9m, distributions maintained at 9.75cpu, occupancy 97.2%, unrealised valuation gain of $60.1m (first gain after three years of losses), $1.4bn of debt refinanced with no maturities before April 2028, gearing 39.6%; FY27 distribution guidance reaffirmed at 9.75cpu
Stock trading around NZ$1.77-1.80, below net tangible assets and analyst price targets

items.notes: Unchanged since FY23; consistent with FY24, FY25 and FY26 actual distributions

items.target: Continued like-for-like growth via CPI-linked (~63% of income) and market rent reviews
items.notes: No specific numeric NPI target disclosed; FY26 NPI grew 9% to $162.2m, HY26 like-for-like growth was 4.0%

items.target: Targeting sustainable AFFO and distribution per unit growth over time
items.notes: Qualitative target only, reiterated at HY26 and FY26; no specific cents-per-unit figure given

items.target: $257.9m committed pipeline ($63.7m remaining to spend) at HY26; ~$2.2bn committed and potential pipeline referenced in FY25 report
items.notes: Coomera Stage 1 activated Feb-26; Macarthur Stage 2 (~A$95.3m) under evaluation for potential CY26 commencement

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Chris Adams (HY26/Q3 FY26): 'Vital's results...are tracking slightly ahead of our expectations, in part due to the strength of the Australian dollar...Vital's underlying business continues to perform well and in line with expectations.' FY25/FY26 outlook commentary notes stabilising property valuations and moderating construction costs, particularly in New Zealand, with Australia recovering more slowly; management remains confident in medium-to-long-term Unit Holder returns supported by demographic tailwinds and the newly internalised, aligned management structure.

bull_case: Internalisation removes acquisition, development and incentive fee leakage to Northwest, is described by management as AFFO- and value-accretive, and better aligns management incentives with Unit Holders
Longest WALE (19 years) of any NZX- or ASX-listed REIT with ~89% of income linked to CPI or structured market reviews provides unusually defensive, escalating income

FY26 marked an inflection - first unrealised property valuation gain ($60.1m) after three consecutive years of revaluation losses, AFFO per unit up 23.5%, and signs that Australian and NZ healthcare property fundamentals are stabilising/improving

Large embedded development pipeline (~$2.2bn) in a structurally undersupplied private healthcare property market, funded by a strengthened, refinanced balance sheet (no debt maturities before April 2028)

Trades at a meaningful discount to NTA per unit (~$2.34-2.47) and below the average analyst price target of ~$2.10, offering potential re-rating upside as internalisation benefits and valuation stabilisation flow through
bear_case: Elevated gearing (~40%) and only partial interest-rate hedging leave the Trust exposed if rates stay higher for longer or cap rates soften again, which could reignite NTA erosion and covenant pressure

Reported net profit/loss is extremely volatile and repeatedly negative (FY23, FY24, HY26 losses) due to non-cash fair-value and derivative movements, making headline earnings unreliable and complicating valuation
Newly internalised management is unproven as a standalone platform; losing Northwest's global scale, relationships and back-office support could pressure execution on developments and leasing
High tenant concentration (top 5 ~65% of rent) and reliance on a small number of hospital operator groups whose own profitability (rent/EBITDAR) is a key swing factor for Vital's income security

Significant AUD/NZD currency exposure (67% of portfolio in Australia) adds translation and distribution volatility, and the $235m internalisation-funding raise diluted existing Unit Holders and pushed NTA per unit down ~6% in HY26
